result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick the sidebar with one page per group and a drill-down list on phones, and both explain why tabs and the long page lose. A gives more you could build from: a narrow form column with full-width tables, a Save button per section, and an Integrations list that opens detail pages. It also explains why it avoids a hamburger menu on phones. B argues better from the content, with points on permissions, merging alerts with notifications, and search, but it is a little inconsistent about the group count and less specific about how the larger groups are laid out. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick the sidebar with one route per group and a drill-down list on phones, and both explain why tabs and the long page lose. B is easier to build from: it widens table groups to the full main area while forms stay in a narrow column, gives each section its own save, puts section-level anchors in deep links, and uses tabs inside a group for the PM. A is also strong, but its grouping is a little inconsistent: it promises 7 to 8 groups, lists 8, and says to put Billing last after listing it second.
